subtitulo: Five questions about a name that points at two places, a 1963 Act, and the answer that is not a verdict
introPt: Late in an evening that was going well, until a word you used turned out to belong to two different maps.
cenario: A table of five people who have been arguing happily for an hour, and who have just turned to the visitor for a ruling.

dialogo.es: Πού πας μετά; Α, στη Μακεδονία; Ποια Μακεδονία;
dialogo.pt: Where are you going next? Ah, to Macedonia? Which Macedonia?
dialogo.tts: Πού πας μετά; Α, στη Μακεδονία; Ποια Μακεδονία;

dialogo.es: Η Μακεδονία είναι εδώ. Πρωτεύουσα η Θεσσαλονίκη.
dialogo.pt: Macedonia is here. Thessaloniki is the capital.
dialogo.tts: Η Μακεδονία είναι εδώ. Πρωτεύουσα η Θεσσαλονίκη.

dialogo.es: Και από την Αγγλία είσαι; Πες μας για τα Γλυπτά, λοιπόν!
dialogo.pt: And you're from England? Go on then, tell us about the Sculptures!
dialogo.tts: Και από την Αγγλία είσαι; Πες μας για τα Γλυπτά, λοιπόν!

dialogo.es: Άσ' τον, βρε. Ούτε εμείς συμφωνούμε μεταξύ μας.
dialogo.pt: Leave him alone. We don't agree among ourselves either.
dialogo.tts: Άσ' τον, βρε. Ούτε εμείς συμφωνούμε μεταξύ μας.

perguntas.pergunta: You say in English that you are going to Macedonia and the table pauses. Why?
opcoes: The word is banned in ordinary conversation
It names a region of northern Greece and is also part of a neighbouring country's constitutional name
It is an archaic term nobody uses any more
You have accidentally taken a side in a war
perguntas.explica: Μακεδονία is a Greek region whose capital is Thessaloniki, and it is also part of the constitutional name fixed by the Prespa Agreement, in force since 12 February 2019. The ambiguity is in the English sentence. Name the city and it disappears.

perguntas.pergunta: Which of these is a dated fact rather than a position?
opcoes: That the Prespa Agreement was fair to both sides
That the name and the history belong to one country
That the ICJ held in 2011 that Greece had breached article 11(1) of the 1995 Interim Accord
That the agreement should never have been signed
perguntas.explica: Case number 142, judgment of 5 December 2011, found the breach over the objection at Bucharest in 2008 and declared the finding itself adequate satisfaction. Whether the agreement was good, fair or legitimate is argued inside both countries and is a position.

perguntas.pergunta: What does section 3 of the British Museum Act 1963 mean for the Parthenon Sculptures?
opcoes: It orders their return once talks conclude
It severely restricts disposal from the collection, so a definitive return would need new legislation
It has been repealed and no longer applies
It applies only to items acquired after 1963
perguntas.explica: Disposal is limited to a short list — duplicates, irreparably damaged items, forgeries, objects unnecessary for study — which the museum's own de-accession policy of November 2018 restates. In November 2025 the talks were described as at an impasse after only a loan was offered.

perguntas.pergunta: Which term is the neutral, descriptive one to use out loud?
opcoes: Elgin Marbles
Parthenon Marbles
Parthenon Sculptures
They are interchangeable and nobody notices
perguntas.explica: The name you choose announces a position before you have argued one. Parthenon Sculptures describes the objects without placing you. Είδα τα Γλυπτά του Παρθενώνα answers a tease with something you did rather than something you think.

perguntas.pergunta: The table asks you to settle their argument. What actually works?
opcoes: Pick the side with the better case, so they know you were listening
Say you do not know enough to judge, then ask how it looks from here
Say all countries have this problem and move on
Refuse to discuss the topic at all
perguntas.explica: Δεν ξέρω αρκετά για να κρίνω is accurate after three weeks, and it is heard as respect. Then πώς το βλέπετε εσείς, or τι άλλαξε εδώ τα τελευταία χρόνια, moves you to the one subject where the person opposite is the only available expert.
